records.text: قطع قصيرة من الحمض النووي DNA تطفو في الدم، تطلقها الخلايا المحتضرة في أنحاء الجسم. معظمها من خلايا طبيعية؛ والجزء الصغير المشتق من الورم (ctDNA) هو ما تلتقطه الخزعات السائلة.

records.text: الحمض النووي الورمي المنتشر (ctDNA) يتكون من شظايا DNA تطلقها الخلايا السرطانية في الدم، ويمكن كشفها بتقنيات تسلسل حساسة.

records.name: cfDNA fragmentomics (ar)
records.text: تقرأ الفراغمنتوميكس أحجام ومواقع شظايا الحمض النووي في الدم، لا الطفرات. تموت الخلايا السرطانية بطريقة غير منظمة وتترك نمط تفتت يمكن التعرف عليه.

records.text: Die Fragmentomik liest die Größe und Position von DNA-Fragmenten im Blut, nicht die Mutationen. Krebszellen sterben unordentlich ab und hinterlassen ein erkennbares Fragmentierungsmuster.

records.name: Lead time in ctDNA monitoring studies (zh)
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) (simple)
records.text: Cell-free DNA is short pieces of DNA floating in the blood shed by dying cells, and the small tumour-derived fraction is what liquid biopsies fish out.

records.name: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) (simple)
records.text: Bits of DNA shed by tumour cells into the blood, detectable with sensitive tests.

records.name: Circulating tumour DNA fraction (and what a negative plasma result means) (simple)
records.text: An estimate of the share of DNA in a blood sample that came from the tumour. A low share can make a negative genetic test harder to interpret.

records.name: Clonal haematopoiesis (CHIP) (simple)
records.text: A group of blood-forming cells with acquired changes can expand. DNA from that group can appear in a blood test and needs to be distinguished from tumour DNA.

records.name: Circulating tumour cell capture (simple)
records.text: Circulating tumour cell capture fishes whole cancer cells out of a blood sample to count or study them, and the count predicts outcome in breast, prostate and colorectal cancer.

records.name: CellSearch circulating tumour cell count (simple)
records.text: A test that counts cells captured and identified under set rules in a blood sample. What the count means depends on the cancer, test and clinical question.

records.name: Parsortix label-free circulating tumour cell harvest (simple)
records.text: Parsortix is a cassette that traps cancer cells from blood by their size and stiffness, then releases them alive for testing, and was the first such device cleared in the US.

records.name: Continuous and near-continuous ctDNA monitoring (simple)
records.text: Taking blood samples more often could change when tumour DNA is first detected. The timing depends on the sampling schedule, and earlier detection alone does not show a survival benefit.

records.name: cfDNA fragmentomics (simple)
records.text: Reading the sizes and positions of DNA pieces in blood. Cancer cells die messily and leave a recognisable pattern.

records.name: Cell-free DNA methylation tests (simple)
records.text: Cell-free DNA methylation tests read chemical marks on DNA fragments shed by tumours into the blood, telling cancer DNA from normal DNA and hinting at where the cancer is.

records.name: Minimal / molecular residual disease (MRD) (simple)
records.text: A test for small amounts of disease after treatment. A negative result means the test found no qualifying signal in that sample; it does not prove that no cancer remains.

records.name: ctDNA MRD positivity (molecular residual disease after curative treatment) (simple)
records.text: A positive residual-disease blood result meets that test's detection rules. Its source and clinical setting matter; it does not guarantee recurrence or show which treatment will help.

records.name: MRD / molecular residual disease testing (simple)
records.text: A residual-disease test looks for a small disease signal after treatment; a negative result does not prove cure, and earlier detection alone does not show that changing treatment helps.

records.name: Tumour-informed versus tumour-naive ctDNA assays (simple)
records.text: One method first selects features from a sampled tumour to track in blood. Another starts with predefined features. Their performance depends on the actual tests, samples and clinical question.

records.name: Flow cytometry (immunophenotyping) (simple)
records.text: Flow cytometry streams cells one by one past lasers and reads the surface markers each carries, which is how leukaemias and lymphomas are typed and residual disease counted.

records.name: ctDNA units, fractions and concentrations (simple)
records.text: A tumour-DNA result needs its unit. A concentration, a share of all measured DNA and a yes-or-no call answer different questions.

records.name: ctDNA and imaging discordance (simple)
records.text: A blood test measures material in a blood sample, while a scan measures a region of the body. Different results need their timing and limits checked before deciding what they mean.

records.name: Lead time in ctDNA monitoring studies (simple)
records.text: The gap between a qualifying positive blood test and a later defined event. It depends on the study rules and sampling schedule and is not extra time added to life.

records.name: Detection and quantification limits (simple)
records.text: A test may find a signal before it can measure the amount reliably. Its limits belong to the stated method and sample conditions.
